title: Excessive data collection at source
description: Parent user shares more data than necessary for authentication (email, password, name, govt ID, six-digit code) - violates data minimization principle
assumptions: Assumes registration requires all these fields

title: Potential lack of lawful basis for data collection
description: Parent user may not be fully informed about why their sensitive data (govt ID, six-digit code) is being collected for authentication purposes
assumptions: Assumes consent may not be explicit or informed

title: Data minimization at destination
description: Authentication service may store more data than necessary for authentication (e.g., government ID, six-digit code) beyond what's needed for login
assumptions: Assumes service stores all registration data

title: Inappropriate information collection
description: Collection of government ID and six-digit code may be disproportionate to authentication needs
assumptions: Assumes these fields are not required for basic authentication

title: Unintended consequences of data storage
description: Stored sensitive data (govt ID, password) could be misused for identity theft or other unauthorized activities
assumptions: Assumes data is stored in a database

title: Data integrity during transmission
description: Sensitive data (password, govt ID) transmitted over network may be intercepted or modified
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted without encryption

title: Unauthorized Access to Parent Account Data
description: Parent account information stored in MongoDB users collection could be accessed by unauthorized parties through database vulnerabilities, misconfiguration, or insider threats, leading to disclosure of sensitive user information.
assumptions: MongoDB is configured with appropriate access controls and encryption at rest

title: Identification of Users via Parent Account Data
description: The authentication service shares parent account information that could be used to identify and profile individual users, potentially enabling tracking and identification across different services.
assumptions: Parent account data contains unique identifiers that can be linked to specific users

title: Linkability via Data Flow Metadata
description: The data flow itself may contain metadata (such as timestamps, IP addresses, or flow patterns) that could be used to link users together or track their authentication activities across different sessions.
assumptions: Data flow metadata is not properly scrubbed or anonymized before transmission

title: Unintended Use of Stored Parent Account Data
description: Parent account information stored in MongoDB users collection may be accessed or used for purposes other than the intended authentication function, such as marketing, analytics, or third-party data sharing without explicit consent.
assumptions: MongoDB access controls are not strictly enforced and data is not properly segregated

title: Unauthorized data sharing with parent user
description: Authentication service may share user data with parent user without proper legal basis or authorization, potentially violating data protection laws.
assumptions: Assumes parent user relationship is legitimate but legal basis for data sharing may not be established.

title: Inaccurate or incomplete user data in JWT
description: User data included in JWT may contain errors, omissions, or outdated information, affecting authentication accuracy and user identification.
assumptions: Assumes JWT is generated from user data without validation checks.

title: Data integrity compromised during transit
description: JWT and user data in transit may be intercepted or modified, potentially altering authentication credentials or user information.
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted without proper encryption or integrity checks.

title: Unintended disclosure of authentication data
description: Data in transit may be exposed to unauthorized parties through network vulnerabilities or interception attacks.
assumptions: Assumes data transmission may not be fully protected against eavesdropping.

title: Improper processing of received authentication data
description: Parent user may mishandle or misuse the received JWT and user data, potentially leading to privacy violations or unauthorized access.
assumptions: Assumes parent user may not have proper security controls for handling authentication data.

title: Unauthorized sharing of parent credentials
description: Child user may share parent email and password without proper legal authority or consent, potentially violating data protection laws regarding minors' data

title: Informed consent not obtained
description: Child may not fully understand the implications of sharing parent authentication credentials, lacking proper informed consent

title: Data interception during authentication
description: Parent email and password in transit could be intercepted by third parties, exposing sensitive authentication credentials

title: Excessive data retention
description: Authentication service may retain more data than necessary for authentication, including parent credentials beyond what's required

title: Unauthorized data processing
description: Authentication service may process parent credentials for purposes beyond authentication, such as profiling or marketing

title: Lawful basis for data sharing
description: Authentication Service may share JWT tokens and child profiles without a clear lawful basis or legal justification for the data transfer.
assumptions: Assumes the authentication service is operating under general privacy regulations

title: Insufficient notice of data sharing
description: Authentication Service may not provide adequate notice to users about what data (JWT, child profiles) is being shared and why.
assumptions: Assumes standard privacy notice practices may not cover this specific data flow

title: Data integrity during transmission
description: JWT tokens and child profiles may be intercepted, modified, or corrupted during transmission from Authentication Service to Child User.
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted over a network without guaranteed integrity protection

title: Unintended disclosure of child data
description: Child profile information may be exposed to unauthorized parties during data transmission, potentially violating child privacy protections.
assumptions: Assumes child profile data contains sensitive personal information

title: Purpose limitation at destination
description: Child User may use JWT and profile data for purposes beyond the original authentication intent, potentially for unauthorized access or profiling.
assumptions: Assumes Child User has control over how received data is used

title: Information quality concerns
description: Child User may receive incomplete, inaccurate, or outdated JWT tokens and profile information, affecting their ability to authenticate properly.
assumptions: Assumes data quality is not guaranteed by the authentication service

title: Lawful basis for sharing child data
description: Parent may share child profile information without proper legal basis or consent from the child (if old enough to consent) or appropriate guardianship verification.
assumptions: Parent may not have proper legal authority or consent documentation

title: Excessive data sharing
description: Parent may share more child data than necessary for profile creation, including sensitive government ID information that could be used for identity theft.
assumptions: Parent may not understand data minimization principles

title: Data integrity during transmission
description: Child profile data in transit may be altered, corrupted, or tampered with during transmission from parent to profile management system.
assumptions: Data may traverse multiple networks or systems

title: Unintended interception of child data
description: Sensitive child information (name, DOB, govt ID) in transit may be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission.
assumptions: Data may traverse public or unsecured networks

title: Lawful processing of child data
description: Child Profile Management process may process child data without proper legal basis or compliance with child privacy regulations.
assumptions: Process may not have proper legal framework for child data processing

title: Data retention beyond necessity
description: Child profile data may be retained longer than necessary for the intended purpose, increasing exposure risk.
assumptions: Process may not have data retention policies

title: Unintended access to child profiles
description: Child profile data stored in the process may be accessed by unauthorized personnel or systems.
assumptions: Process may not have adequate access controls

title: Data Integrity - Child Profile Corruption
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB could be corrupted, altered, or tampered with during storage, leading to inaccurate or misleading information about children.
assumptions: Assumes MongoDB storage mechanisms are properly configured and monitored for data integrity.

title: Data Availability - Child Profile Inaccessibility
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB could become unavailable or inaccessible due to system failures, storage issues, or intentional denial of access, preventing authorized parties from accessing critical child information.
assumptions: Assumes MongoDB storage mechanisms are properly configured and monitored for data availability.

title: Data Confidentiality - Unauthorized Access to Child Profiles
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB could be accessed by unauthorized parties, potentially exposing sensitive information about children including personal details, health information, or behavioral data.
assumptions: Assumes MongoDB access controls and authentication mechanisms are properly configured.

title: Data Accuracy - Incomplete or Outdated Child Profile Information
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB could be inaccurate, incomplete, or outdated, leading to incorrect information about children that could impact decision-making or care.
assumptions: Assumes data entry and update processes are properly validated and monitored.

title: Data Minimization - Excessive Personal Information Collection
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB could include more personal information than necessary for the intended purpose, potentially exposing unnecessary sensitive information about children.
assumptions: Assumes data collection practices follow data minimization principles.

title: Data Retention - Excessive Child Profile Data Retention
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB could be retained longer than necessary, increasing the risk of data breaches and privacy violations over extended periods.
assumptions: Assumes data retention policies are properly implemented and enforced.

title: Data Linkage - Child Profile Data Correlation
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB could be linked with other data sources to identify individuals, potentially enabling re-identification or profiling of children.
assumptions: Assumes MongoDB data is properly isolated and access is restricted.

title: Child User Identification Risk
description: Child user's search patterns, likes, and comments may be used to identify or profile the child beyond their stated identity, potentially violating child privacy protections.
assumptions: Assumes child user may not be fully aware of how their data is being used for identification purposes.

title: Child Data Collection Lawfulness
description: Collection and sharing of child user data for video search and interaction may not comply with child-specific privacy laws (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K).
assumptions: Assumes child user may be under 13 years old and subject to stricter privacy regulations.

title: Child User Re-identification Risk
description: Video Management Service may re-identify the child user from search patterns, interaction history, and behavioral data, creating persistent profiles.
assumptions: Assumes service maintains user profiles and correlates multiple data points.

title: Child Data Quality Concerns
description: Video search and interaction data may be inaccurate or incomplete, affecting the quality of services provided to the child user.
assumptions: Assumes data collection mechanisms may have errors or gaps.

title: Child Privacy Non-compliance
description: Video Management Service may not comply with child-specific privacy requirements, including consent mechanisms and data minimization.
assumptions: Assumes service may not have implemented age-appropriate privacy controls.

title: Data Flow Identification Risk
description: Meta-data in the data flow (e.g., timestamps, IP addresses, device information) may be used to link or identify the child user across different services.
assumptions: Assumes data flow includes technical metadata that could be correlated with user identity.

title: Lawful basis for video data collection unclear
description: The Video Management Service may collect and share video metadata and files without a clear lawful basis under GDPR or other applicable privacy regulations. The legal justification for processing this data may be insufficient or not properly documented.

title: Excessive video data collection
description: The Video Management Service may collect more video metadata and files than necessary for the intended purpose, violating data minimization principles. This could include collecting unnecessary personal identifiers or excessive video content.

title: Insufficient notification to data subjects
description: Users may not be adequately informed about how their video data is collected, stored, and shared. Privacy notices may be incomplete or not easily accessible.

title: Inadequate data retention and deletion policies
description: The MongoDB videos collection may lack clear policies for data retention periods and secure deletion of video metadata and files. This could lead to unnecessary long-term storage of sensitive data.

title: Unintended data exposure through MongoDB
description: The MongoDB data store may have security vulnerabilities that could lead to unintended exposure of video metadata and files to unauthorized parties, including potential data breaches.

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
description: The storage of video metadata and files in MongoDB may not fully comply with applicable data protection regulations, including encryption requirements, access controls, and audit logging.

title: Lawful basis for collecting child search and watch history
description: The collection of child search and watch history may lack a clear lawful basis under privacy regulations, especially given the sensitive nature of child data.
assumptions: Assumes no explicit legal framework or consent mechanism is documented for this data collection.

title: Excessive data collection for child profile
description: Collecting comprehensive search and watch history may be more extensive than necessary for the stated purpose of child profile management, potentially violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Assumes the purpose is limited to child profile management without additional legitimate uses.

title: Insufficient notification of data collection
description: Children and parents may not be adequately informed about what data is being collected, how it will be used, and their rights regarding this data.
assumptions: Assumes notification mechanisms exist but may not be comprehensive or understandable.

title: Inadequate data retention and destruction policies
description: Child search and watch history may be retained indefinitely without a clear retention schedule, increasing the risk of data breaches and long-term privacy violations.
assumptions: Assumes no documented data retention policy exists for this collection.

title: Inappropriate data storage practices
description: Storing child search and watch history in MongoDB may expose sensitive data to security vulnerabilities if access controls are not properly implemented.
assumptions: Assumes MongoDB instance may have standard security configurations that need verification.

title: Potential non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Storage of child search and watch history may not comply with specific child privacy regulations such as COPPA or GDPR-K, which have stricter requirements for child data.
assumptions: Assumes jurisdiction may involve child-specific privacy regulations.

title: User Identification Through Video Metadata
description: Parent user may inadvertently reveal personal identifying information through video metadata (timestamps, location, device information) during upload.
assumptions: Video upload process may capture or transmit metadata that can be used to identify the user.

title: Potential Unlawful Content Upload
description: Parent user may upload content that violates laws or platform policies, creating legal and compliance risks.
assumptions: User may not be fully aware of content restrictions or may intentionally upload prohibited material.

title: Data Flow Metadata Linkage
description: Metadata about the parties (parent user and video management service) in the data flow could be used to link or identify them.
assumptions: Network traffic may contain metadata that reveals communication patterns and identities.

title: User Identification from Stored Video Data
description: Video management service may identify parent user from video content, metadata, or associated account information during storage and processing.
assumptions: Service may collect and retain user identification data alongside video content.

title: Insufficient Notification of Data Processing
description: Parent user may not be adequately notified about how their video data will be processed, stored, and used by the video management service.
assumptions: Privacy notices may be incomplete or users may not understand data processing implications.

title: Video Data Quality Compromise
description: Video management service may compromise data quality during upload, approval, or rejection processes.
assumptions: Processing may introduce errors, corruption, or loss of video data integrity.

title: Lawful basis for video sharing
description: The Video Management Service may share video content without a clear lawful basis or adequate consent from the child's guardians, potentially violating data protection laws.

title: Video content integrity at source
description: The Video Management Service may not ensure the integrity of video content before sharing, potentially allowing tampered or malicious content to be distributed to the child.

title: Metadata leakage during transmission
description: Data in transit may contain metadata about the parties (source and destination) that could be used to link or identify the child user, even if the video content itself is anonymized.

title: Unintended consequences of video viewing
description: The child user may experience unintended consequences from viewing the video content, such as psychological impact, inappropriate content exposure, or behavioral changes.

title: Data integrity at destination
description: The child user may receive corrupted or tampered video content due to transmission issues or interception, affecting the quality and safety of the received data.

title: Non-compliance with child data protection laws
description: Collection and storage of child browsing data may violate COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child-specific privacy regulations without proper consent mechanisms and safeguards.
assumptions: Assumes the data collection lacks explicit parental consent and appropriate safeguards for minors' data.

title: Inference of sensitive characteristics from browsing patterns
description: Child browsing data may be used to infer sensitive attributes about children (interests, preferences, vulnerabilities) that could lead to inappropriate targeting or profiling.
assumptions: Assumes browsing patterns contain enough information to make sensitive inferences about children.

title: Lawful basis for data collection unclear
description: The legal basis for collecting and processing child browsing data may not be properly established, potentially violating data protection principles.
assumptions: Assumes the organization has not clearly documented the lawful basis for this data collection.

title: Data in transit could be intercepted and linked
description: Meta-data about the parties (source and destination) in the data flow could be used to link or identify children, especially if transmitted over unencrypted channels.
assumptions: Assumes data may be transmitted without proper encryption or with insufficient security controls.

title: AI processing may impact children's dignity and development
description: AI recommendation engine processing child browsing data could make inappropriate recommendations that affect children's development, interests, or dignity.
assumptions: Assumes the AI system may not have appropriate safeguards for child-specific content recommendations.

title: Lack of notification about AI data usage
description: Children and parents may not be adequately informed about how their browsing data will be used by the AI recommendation engine.
assumptions: Assumes current notification practices do not specifically address AI data usage for children.

title: Unintended consequences from AI recommendations
description: AI-generated recommendations based on child browsing data could have unintended negative consequences for children (e.g., inappropriate content, harmful suggestions).
assumptions: Assumes the AI system may not have appropriate content filtering or safety mechanisms.

title: Sharing browsing data without adequate legal basis
description: The AI Recommendation Engine may be sharing browsing data to third-party advertisers without a clear legal basis or adequate consent from users, potentially violating data protection laws.
assumptions: Assumes browsing data is being collected and shared without explicit user consent or legal justification.

title: Insufficient notice to users about data sharing
description: Users may not be adequately informed that their browsing data will be shared with third-party advertisers, violating transparency requirements.
assumptions: Assumes users are not explicitly notified about the data sharing practice.

title: Data integrity risk during transmission
description: Browsing data in transit between the AI Recommendation Engine and third-party advertisers could be intercepted, modified, or tampered with, compromising data integrity.
assumptions: Assumes data transmission may not be adequately secured or encrypted.

title: Unintended consequences from data metadata
description: Metadata about the data flow (e.g., timing, frequency, volume) could be used to link or identify users, creating unintended privacy risks.
assumptions: Assumes metadata could be captured and analyzed by third parties.

title: Third-party data minimization concerns
description: Third-party advertisers may collect and store more browsing data than necessary for their advertising purposes, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Assumes advertisers may not be bound by strict data minimization requirements.

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
description: Third-party advertisers may not be compliant with applicable data protection laws regarding the receipt, processing, and storage of browsing data.
assumptions: Assumes third-party advertisers operate in jurisdictions with varying data protection standards.

title: Excessive Data Collection at Source
description: Authentication Service may collect more government ID images than necessary for authentication purposes, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Assumes the service collects all available ID images without filtering for necessity.

title: Potential Lawfulness Issues
description: The collection and sharing of government ID images may lack clear legal basis or proper consent from data subjects.
assumptions: Assumes the service operates without explicit legal authorization for this data handling.

title: Insufficient Notice to Data Subjects
description: Users may not be adequately informed about what government ID images are being collected, why, and how they will be used.
assumptions: Assumes the service does not provide clear privacy notices to users.

title: Metadata Exposure During Transmission
description: Data flow may expose metadata about the parties involved (e.g., timestamps, file names, headers) that could be used to link or identify individuals.
assumptions: Assumes standard file transmission protocols that may leak metadata.

title: Unintended Access to Stored Images
description: Stored government ID images may be accessed by unauthorized personnel or systems, leading to privacy violations.
assumptions: Assumes the file system lacks adequate access controls.

title: Inadequate Data Minimization at Storage
description: The file system may store government ID images without proper retention policies or deletion mechanisms, leading to unnecessary data retention.
assumptions: Assumes the storage system lacks automated retention and deletion policies.

title: Non-compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: Storage of government ID images may not comply with applicable privacy laws and regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA, or national privacy laws).
assumptions: Assumes the storage practices do not meet all legal requirements.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored JWT
description: JWT tokens stored in browser localStorage can be accessed by any JavaScript on the page, including malicious scripts, leading to potential unauthorized access to authentication credentials and user session data.
assumptions: Assumes localStorage is accessible to any script on the page, which is a fundamental characteristic of browser storage.

title: Excessive Data Sharing of JWT
description: Authentication service may share more data in the JWT than necessary for authentication, potentially including sensitive user information that could be exposed if the token is compromised.
assumptions: Assumes JWT may contain claims beyond minimal authentication requirements.

title: JWT Metadata in Transit
description: JWT tokens in transit may contain metadata about the parties involved (source and destination) that could be used to link or identify users across different sessions or services.
assumptions: Assumes JWT contains claims that could be used for user identification or linking.

title: Unlawful or unauthorized sharing of child history data
description: The Child Profile Management process may share child history data without proper legal basis, consent from the child (if of age), or appropriate parental authorization.
assumptions: Assumes child history data contains sensitive personal information requiring strict legal compliance.

title: Excessive data retrieval - data minimization violation
description: The process may retrieve more child history data than necessary for the parent review purpose, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Assumes the process has discretion over what data to retrieve.

title: Inaccurate or incomplete child history data
description: The child history data retrieved may contain errors, omissions, or outdated information that could mislead the parent.
assumptions: Assumes the data collection and storage processes may introduce errors.

title: Unintended disclosure during data transmission
description: Child history data in transit may be intercepted by unauthorized parties through network vulnerabilities or man-in-the-middle attacks.
assumptions: Assumes the data transmission channel may not be fully secured.

title: Unintended disclosure by parent user
description: The parent user may share or disclose the retrieved child history data to unauthorized third parties.
assumptions: Assumes the parent user may not be bound by appropriate privacy obligations.

title: Non-compliant use of child history data
description: The parent user may use the child history data in ways not intended or authorized (e.g., for purposes other than parental review).
assumptions: Assumes the parent user may not fully understand or follow intended data use policies.
